rics.description: JOB VACANCIES - PARTIAL CITIES
rics.meaning: Job Vacancies (Partial Cities) — partial measure of job-vacancy stocks across major Chinese cities. Less comprehensive than a true national vacancy series.
rics.how_to_use: Indicative. Use alongside JV-to-applicants ratio (separately published) for labor-demand pulse. Falls during recessions.

rics.how_to_use: Annual frequency. Use monthly survey rate (aCNCNUERLM) for high-frequency tracking.

rics.meaning: China Employment: Unemployment, Urban area, Quarterly, Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, China. Sectoral or sub-aggregate employment data.

rics.description: Urban registered unemployment rate
rics.meaning: Urban Registered Unemployment Rate — legacy unemployment measure tracking only people who registered for unemployment benefits at local labor bureaus. Pre-2018 official headline; less meaningful now (people often don't bother registering).
rics.how_to_use: Use the survey rate (aCNCNUERLM) instead. Urban-registered rate runs much lower (~3-4%) than the broader survey rate (5-6%) because registration is incomplete.

rics.description: Urban survey unemployment rate
rics.meaning: Urban Survey Unemployment Rate — the official monthly headline unemployment rate, based on the urban-area labor-force survey. Replaced the old urban-registered unemployment rate as the headline gauge in 2018.
rics.how_to_use: THE China unemployment headline. Pre-COVID ~5%; spiked to 6.2% in 2020 and 2022 (lockdowns). Released monthly. Youth unemployment (16-24 yo, separately published) is much higher (~17-21%) — a major political concern; NBS suspended the youth series in mid-2023 then resumed with revised methodology.

rics.description: Wages, urban employees, manufacturing
rics.meaning: China Wages: Wages, urban employees, manufacturing. Wage data by sector or category.
rics.how_to_use: China publishes wages by urban formal-sector (above-designated-size firms). Migrant worker wages tracked separately by Ministry of Human Resources. Real-wage growth tracks productivity + inflation; recent slowdown reflects deflation.

rics.description: Employment, Labour Force Survey, Standardized (based on source annual data)
rics.meaning: Employment, Labour Force Survey — standardized total-employment level. ~750M employed.
rics.how_to_use: Compare to labor force for unemployment rate. China labor force has been shrinking since 2014 (peak ~810M) due to demographic transition — a major structural macro story.
